### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via MessagingService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via EmitInput (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78ddf37931f2307c79889b5ae797154732fadf55` — the merge of head `c8bc3f137222e4866a4d3c2a95042b73d57b4eac` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78ddf37931f2307c79889b5ae797154732fadf55 && git checkout 78ddf37931f2307c79889b5ae797154732fadf55
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 c8bc3f137222e4866a4d3c2a95042b73d57b4eac && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff c8bc3f137222e4866a4d3c2a95042b73d57b4eac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9dd0b1eaa5f83be7cddf56b9f17736150d3f9d25`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (no hits; owed by the security#1 hand-off) + packages/services/service-messaging/src/recipient-resolver.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- Exported surface of `@objectstack/service-messaging`: unchanged. `Audience`, `AudienceSpec`, `EmitInput`, `ResolveContext` keep their shapes; no export added or removed; `role:NAME` is still an accepted selector. Right.
- `RecipientResolver.resolveRole`: the organization is now required, and the membership read always carries it. This matches what `main` already declares (`AudienceSpec` TSDoc: `role:NAME` names the emitting organization's members holding that role; class summary: tenant-scoped). Right.
- `MessagingService.emit` step 3: the resolver is handed the `owned` organization (the producer's, else the stored event row's). For `role:` this is the declared rule. Right.
- The same line also moves `org:members`: it now resolves in the stored event row's organization when the producer names none. The PR derives and declares this for `role:` only. Wrong as declared — see ④ finding 1.
- Check-runs on this head: all concluded runs are success or skipped; `Check Changeset` had one success, one cancelled and one still in progress at read time. No red gate.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-messaging` matches a fix in a released package with no protocol kind; the changeset carries both declaration lines.
- `Clause-②: no` is right for the `role:` change; neither `(narrowing)` nor a breaking marker is owed: no published accept set narrows (selector grammar and types are unchanged), and the resolved set is pulled back to the contract `main` already declares.
- "Who moves" is sufficient for `role:`. It is not sufficient for the diff as a whole: it does not name the `org:members` move, and "exactly as `org:members` already behaves" is no longer true of the fallback this PR adds. See ④ finding 1.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds only if `org:members` keeps its documented reading; if the move is kept, re-judge the kind.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, `Clause-②: no` left for the review: answered in ② — `no` stands for `role:`.
- Dev flag, the `emit` step 3b preference filter still reads with the producer's organization: acceptable to leave in this PR (it only removes or defers recipient/channel pairs, never adds one, and is unchanged from `main`). Accepted deviation, follow-up owed to the security#1 seat (④ nit 3).
- Seat note, file surface widened by one service-automation test file: that file is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; not reviewed here.
- No `open_questions` entry is present.

### ④ Design judgment

`recipient-resolver.ts` — holds. `resolveRole` is the only reader of the `role:` selector; every path through it either returns nobody before any read or reads with the organization. Absent and empty organization both resolve to nobody with a warning; the rest of an audience still resolves; a failed read still resolves to nobody. The TSDoc on `ResolveContext.organizationId`, the class summary and the method agree with the code.

`messaging-service.ts` — the `role:` half holds; one must-fix.

1. **must-fix** — `MessagingService.emit` step 3 and the type TSDoc in the same file. Handing the resolver the `owned` organization also changes `org:members`: an emit whose producer names no organization now resolves `org:members` in the stored event row's organization, where `main` resolves it to nobody. That contradicts, on this head, the `EmitInput.organizationId` TSDoc ("nobody when this is absent") and the `AudienceSpec` TSDoc in this file, and on `main` the published text in `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` (notify recipients paragraph) and `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` (the `org:members` bullet). It is not named in the title, the body's rule for who moves, or the changeset's "Who moves", and no test pins it. Required, one of:
   - (a) keep `org:members` on the producer-named organization in `emit` step 3, so the diff changes `role:` alone as declared; or
   - (b) keep the move and own it: correct the two TSDoc blocks in `messaging-service.ts`, add the pin for `org:members` on the event-row organization, name it in the changeset's "Who moves" and drop "exactly as `org:members` already behaves", re-judge `Metadata-protocol:`, and file the docs and skills follow-up for the two published passages.
2. **nit** — `.changeset/messaging-role-audience-emitting-organization.md`, first sentence: it states the rule for "an emit's audience"; name the selectors this diff binds instead. Prose face only.
3. **nit (accepted deviation, follow-up owed)** — `MessagingService.emit` step 3b: the preference filter is left on the producer's organization while step 3 uses the `owned` one. Unchanged behaviour; follow-up to the security#1 seat rather than a change on this head.
4. **nit** — `messaging-service.test.ts`: the event-row fallback is pinned against the file's engine double only; a pin on the real engine's derived organization would sit better beside the existing `notification-organization-follows-event` integration file. Follow-up.

The must-fix earns a delta review of its fix by this seat.

The new pin and its control in `messaging-service.test.ts` would go red if `org:members` followed the event row again.

Attempts to break it (empty and non-string organization values, an empty role name, case or padding differences, a single non-array audience, mixed audiences, the dedup short-circuits) all resolve as on `main` or as the declared rule.

1. **nit (follow-up)** — `MessagingService.resolveAudience`, per-spec branch: it hands the resolver a bare spec where the single-call branch hands it the list, so an audience entry outside the `AudienceSpec` type is not read identically by the two branches. Required: pass a one-entry list. No typed audience and no first-party producer is affected; follow-up card, not a change on this head.
2. **nit** — PR body, prose face only: the rule paragraph, the `messaging-service.ts` bullet and the test list still describe round 1. Bring them to this head's rule.
3. **nit (carried)** — round-1 nits 3 and 4 remain accepted deviations with follow-ups owed.

Nits alone; the round ends here.
